html:
A Mende rice farmer from what is now Sierra Leone, captured in 1839 and shipped to Cuba, who led the revolt on the Spanish schooner La Amistad that July.

The captives killed the captain and ordered the crew to sail them to Africa; instead the ship zigzagged north and was seized off Long Island by the US Navy. A long court fight followed, and in 1841 the US Supreme Court, hearing John Quincy Adams for the Africans, ruled that they had been illegally enslaved and were free. Sengbe Pieh and the other survivors returned to Sierra Leone in 1842. He is a national hero there. See also the slave trade.
